note: Algorithm identities, versions, and tuning constants as DATA rather than code (plan §9 'AlgorithmVersion gains a bundled registry file', §15 'algorithm constants/params live in packages/contracts/algorithms/algorithms.json'). The intent is that the duplicated cross-platform logic stays inside D-4's budget as curve evaluation only — never as two hand-copied constant tables that silently drift. Every entry mirrors the AlgorithmVersion domain type (algorithmId, semver, params, introducedIn); params is numeric-only because AlgorithmVersion.params is [String: Double] on iOS and Map<String, Double> on Kotlin — non-numeric metadata lives in sibling fields (producesMetricIds, inputMetricIds, paramNotes, and the baseline entry's structured windowTable), never inside params. This file is shipped in-app and versioned with the app: plan §15 explicitly rules out remote configuration so an algorithm change is always an app update with a changelog, never a silent behaviour change pushed at a user. Bumping a constant is a semver bump and a new AlgorithmVersion row — derived values are append-only (I2), so old rows keep referencing the old semver and are never rewritten.
status: WHAT IS WIRED, AS OF PHASE 0. Both platforms LOAD this file: apps/ios/Sources/Ontology/AlgorithmRegistry.swift and apps/android/.../ontology/AlgorithmRegistry.kt read the bundled mirror and resolve an entry to a frozen AlgorithmVersion, each covered by a test (AlgorithmRegistryTests / AlgorithmRegistryTest) that loads the real asset and asserts a known id, semver and param. Nothing EVALUATES these curves yet — the Phase-2 score engines are the consumers, and until they land no DerivedValue in the app is computed from a constant in this file. That distinction is the point: an earlier revision of this note claimed both platforms already loaded the file and that 'the loading path is fixed in Phase 0', when neither platform had a loader at all and nothing anywhere referenced algorithms.json. Because the sync scripts mirrored it into both bundles and CI gated the mirrors for drift, the file read as load-bearing at review while being inert (audit finding #5). If you delete either AlgorithmRegistry, or let its tests go, correct this paragraph in the same change rather than leaving the claim standing.
provisionalMeans: Entries marked provisional=true have NOT had their constants validated against data. They exist so the ids and the param SCHEMA are fixed in Phase 0 and the Phase-2 engines tune numbers rather than invent structure. A provisional algorithm sets DerivedValue.provisional = true on every row it produces, so the surface can say so.

levels.provisional: Constants are a stated default, not yet validated against data. Derived values computed with a provisional algorithm set DerivedValue.provisional = true.
levels.stable: Constants validated and published in docs/algorithms/. Changing one requires a semver bump.

algorithms.summaryEn: Personal-normal band as a robust median with a median-absolute-deviation spread over a per-metric trailing window. Log-normal vitals (HRV) are banded in the log domain; MAD-based outlier rejection removes single wild readings before the band is drawn; the band stays provisional until it has enough points to be honest about.

paramNotes.windowDays: The DEFAULT trailing window in days for any baseline-eligible metric without an explicit windowTable rule. Overridden per metric by windowTable — HRV 60d, RHR/RR/temp 14d, sleep-need inputs 28d (plan §18). Published rationale in docs/algorithms/baselines.md.
paramNotes.madToSigma: Standard consistency constant making MAD comparable to a normal-distribution sigma. Not tunable — changing it changes what the band means.
paramNotes.minPoints: Below this many in-window daily points the baseline stays provisional=true rather than showing a confident band on thin data. A provisional baseline is never presented as a score.
paramNotes.bandSigmas: Half-width of the personal band in sigmas (as estimated by madToSigma * MAD). 1.0 keeps the band at roughly one robust standard deviation either side of centre.
paramNotes.outlierMadThreshold: A daily point more than this many MADs from the in-window median is rejected before the band is drawn, so one artefactual reading (a bad HRV sample after a late meal, a sensor spike) cannot move the personal normal. Rejection is skipped when MAD is exactly 0 — a zero spread cannot define an outlier, and a lone differing value in an otherwise-flat window is data, not noise. 3.5 follows the Iglewicz–Hoaglin modified-z convention.
paramNotes.establishingFraction: The baseline clears 'provisional' only once it has at least minPoints AND at least this fraction of its window filled (plan §18: 'n>=7 and >=half the window'). For a 60d HRV window this means 30 days before HRV is treated as established from a cold start; a first-connect history backfill can clear it on day one.
paramNotes.retroactiveGraceDays: A per-day derived score computed more than this many days after the day it describes was 'computed later from history' (e.g. a readiness day recomputed once an import backfilled that week). It is surfaced with the retroactive quality label rather than as a live reading. See docs/algorithms/baselines.md for why this is a read-time-derived label, not a stored column.
paramNotes.supersedesSemver: 1.0.0 (a single 14-day linear window) remains valid for every baseline row already computed with it. Per I2 those rows are never rewritten; the semver on the row is what explains it, and a later recompute appends a 2.0.0 row rather than mutating the old one.

algorithms.summaryEn: Time asleep as a share of time in bed.
Personal baseline duration + a decayed share of accumulated debt + a prior-day effort allowance, minus credit for naps. Emitted as a range, never a fake-exact minutes target (plan §4 principle 9).

paramNotes.debtRepaymentFraction: PROVISIONAL. Share of outstanding debt folded into tonight's need; the rest carries forward. Prevents a large debt from producing an unreachable target that only shames the user.
paramNotes.effortFactorSecondsPerPoint: PROVISIONAL. Extra sleep need per point of effort.day. Depends on the effort scale, which is A3-pending — re-derive if A3 chooses 0-21.
paramNotes.rangeHalfWidthSeconds: The +/- half-width of the displayed range. Widened by the engine when input completeness is low.
paramNotes.minNeedSeconds: Floor/ceiling clamps exist so a sparse-data user is never shown an absurd need. They are display honesty, not a recommendation.

algorithms.summaryEn: Actual sleep as a share of estimated need, bounded, shown as a range when the need estimate's confidence is low.

paramNotes.upperBoundPercent: Capped so oversleeping does not read as an unbounded score. Values above the cap are stored uncapped and clamped at the presentation edge only.
paramNotes.lowConfidenceThreshold: Below this input-completeness confidence the value renders as a band, not a point.

algorithms.summaryEn: Rolling accumulator of (need - actual), decaying exponentially so old shortfalls stop counting rather than accumulating forever.

paramNotes.decayHalfLifeDays: PROVISIONAL. Without decay a single bad fortnight would follow a user for months, which is neither true nor wellness-safe.
paramNotes.maxDebtSeconds: Clamp so the surface cannot display an alarming, ever-growing number.

algorithms.summaryEn: 0-100 from the variance of bed and wake times across a trailing window; tighter timing scores higher.

paramNotes.zeroScoreStdevSeconds: PROVISIONAL. The timing spread that maps to 0. 3h chosen so ordinary weekend drift does not floor the score.
paramNotes.minNights: Below this the value is provisional=true rather than scoring someone on two nights of data.

algorithms.summaryEn: Count of wake-stage episodes lasting at least a threshold duration.

paramNotes.minEpisodeSeconds: PROVISIONAL. Below this a wake episode is stage-classifier noise, not something the sleeper experienced.
paramNotes.mergeGapSeconds: Two wake episodes closer than this are one disturbance, so classifier flapping does not inflate the count.

algorithms.summaryEn: 0-100 composite of how much you slept against your own need, how regular your timing was, and how unbroken the night stayed. Weighted toward duration adequacy, with regularity carrying real weight because timing regularity predicts long-run outcomes at least as well as duration. Renormalised over whichever components exist, and never produced at all without a performance term.

paramNotes.performanceWeight: PROVISIONAL. Duration against personal need is the dominant term; a score that ignored it would not be a sleep score.
paramNotes.consistencyWeight: PROVISIONAL. Deliberately large for a secondary term: sleep regularity is at least as predictive of long-run outcomes as duration (UK Biobank, SLEEP 2024), so weighting it as a rounding error would misrepresent the evidence.
paramNotes.continuityWeight: PROVISIONAL. Smallest weight because disturbance counts are the least reliable input - nil entirely without stage data, and sensitive to how a source segments awakenings.
paramNotes.disturbanceZeroScoreCount: PROVISIONAL. Disturbance count at which the continuity term reaches 0.
paramNotes.performanceCapPercent: Performance is stored uncapped (sleeping 130% of need is real); the SCORE caps it at 100 so oversleeping cannot buy down a poor consistency term.

algorithms.degradationNotes: Requires sleep.performance, which is nil until a personal sleep-duration baseline exists - so a new install has no score rather than a fabricated one. Consistency (nil below the consistency minimum) and disturbances (nil without stage data) are each dropped from the weighted mean and the remaining weights renormalised, with the result marked provisional whenever any component is absent.

algorithms.summaryEn: Weighted composite of each input's z-position against its own personal baseline, mapped to 0-100. Reduced-input variants drop a term and redistribute its weight rather than substituting a default.

paramNotes.weightHrv: PROVISIONAL, pending A3. BADAN's OWN launch weights (HRV 0.5, RHR 0.2, RR 0.1, sleep 0.2 — plan §11 EPIC-25), deliberately NOT WHOOP's claimed weights; the rationale and citations belong in docs/algorithms/readiness.md when EPIC-25 lands. Weights must sum to 1.0 across present inputs; the engine renormalizes over whatever is available.
paramNotes.zClampSigmas: Clamps each input's z before weighting so one wild reading (a bad HRV sample after a late meal) cannot dominate the composite.
paramNotes.minInputsToScoreAtAll: Below this no score is emitted at all. An honest absence beats a confident number built from one input.
paramNotes.supersedesSemver: 1.0.0 remains valid for every row already computed with it. Per I2 those rows are never rewritten; the version on the row is what explains it.

algorithms.summaryEn: Log-curve accumulation over time spent in each heart-rate zone, relative to the user's max HR. Monotonic: more time or higher zones never lower the score.

paramNotes.scaleMax: A3-PENDING. Plan §28 A3 has not chosen between a 0-21 log scale (WHOOP-familiar) and 0-100 (consistent with every other BADAN score). The registry id and canonical unit are scale-independent by design, so resolving A3 changes scaleMax and the zone weights here plus a display unit — it does NOT change effort.day's metric id or force a data migration.
paramNotes.hrMaxConstant: Default maximum heart rate = hrMaxConstant - hrMaxAgeCoefficient * age (Tanaka 2001: 208 - 0.7*age), used only when the user has not set their own HR max in profile. The profile value always wins; editing it triggers an append-only historical recompute (EPIC-26, I2). A default, never a measured maximum.
paramNotes.hrMaxAgeCoefficient: See hrMaxConstant. Together they seed the zone edges the zoneNFloorPctHrMax percentages are taken against.
paramNotes.zone1Weight: PROVISIONAL. Roughly geometric so the curve rewards intensity without letting a single hard interval swamp a long easy day.
paramNotes.logCurveK: PROVISIONAL. Curve steepness. Must keep the accumulation monotonic in both time and zone — EPIC-26 asserts this as a property test.
paramNotes.zone1FloorPctHrMax: Default zone edges as a percentage of max HR. The user can edit zone edges in profile; edited zones override these and are stored per-user, not here.

algorithms.summaryEn: The effort.day curve applied over a single session's window instead of the day.

paramNotes.scaleMax: A3-PENDING — must stay identical to effort.day's scaleMax or a workout's effort would not be comparable with the day it sits inside.
paramNotes.sparseHrFallbackMinSamplesPerMinute: Below this HR sample density the engine emits the labelled reduced-input 'activity load' variant instead of a zone-based score. A user whose watch did not record continuous HR must never be shown a zero — that reads as failure, not as missing data.

algorithms.summaryEn: A DAILY direction of autonomic load, read from DAYTIME heart-rate-variability sampling against the person's own recent daytime pattern — never a live or instantaneous number. A density detector decides first whether anything may be said at all: below the published samples-per-hour gate the surface is hidden with an explanation about the device's sampling, because an Apple-Watch-class wearable does not record daytime HRV densely enough to support a real-time stress index.

paramNotes.semverNote: 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 (EPIC-34). The 0.1.0 params were a Phase-0 placeholder schema (minSamplesPerHour/minCoveredHours/smoothingHalfLifeHours) seeded before the engine existed; no StressEngine ever loaded them, so no DerivedValue anywhere carries stress.day_trend@0.1.0. The bump is still recorded rather than edited in place, because a shipped 0.2.0 bundle contained those constants and I2 auditability is only worth anything if version ids are never quietly reused.
paramNotes.densityWindowDays: Trailing local days the density detector measures over. A week, so a couple of unusual days (a flight, a day the watch was off the wrist) cannot flip the surface state on their own.
paramNotes.denseMinSamplesPerHour: PROVISIONAL. At or above this DAYTIME sampling rate (samples per waking hour, sleep windows excluded) the data is vendor-grade continuous — roughly a reading every 15 minutes — which is the only density that could support the full intraday index. Reachable in practice only from a continuously-sampling vendor (Oura/Garmin/Samsung, Phase 4); the intraday index itself is NOT implemented in Phase 3, so a dense-classified surface still renders the daily trend and says the intraday view is not available yet.
paramNotes.moderateMinSamplesPerHour: PROVISIONAL. The floor for saying anything at all: at least one daytime HRV reading per two waking hours. Below it the surface is HIDDEN with an explanation — the plan's 'biggest false-precision trap' guard. Apple-Watch-only users typically sit around 0.1/hr and are therefore hidden by default, which is a fact about the device's sampling, not a failure of the user or of BADAN.
paramNotes.minDaysWithDaytimeSamples: Of densityWindowDays, how many must carry at least one daytime sample. Stops one dense day (a session of guided-breathing readings) from unlocking a surface the rest of the week cannot support.
paramNotes.minDaytimeHoursInWindow: Total waking hours the window must contain before a samples-per-hour rate is meaningful at all. Guards the denominator: three samples in one waking hour is 3.0/hr arithmetically and evidence of nothing.
paramNotes.minDaytimeSamplesPerDay: Below this many daytime samples a DAY contributes no value to the trend (it is a gap, never imputed). One reading is a point, not a day's central tendency.
paramNotes.referenceWindowDays: Trailing window of daily daytime values the personal reference (robust centre + spread) is taken over. Deliberately NOT the heart.hrv baseline from EPIC-23: that baseline is dominated by overnight readings, and overnight HRV runs systematically higher than daytime HRV, so reading a daytime value against it would report 'elevated load' every single day. The reference is daytime-vs-daytime or it is nothing.
paramNotes.minReferenceDays: Below this many daily values in the reference window there is no personal daytime pattern to read against, and the surface is hidden as STILL LEARNING — a calibration fact, distinct from the device-sparsity explanation.
paramNotes.trendWindowDays: The sliding window the published trend value is computed over. The output describes a WINDOW ENDING on its day, never a moment.
paramNotes.minTrendDays: Minimum daily values present inside trendWindowDays before a trend is emitted. Missing days stay gaps.
paramNotes.trendHalfLifeDays: Exponential recency weighting inside the trend window: a day's weight is 0.5^(ageInDays / trendHalfLifeDays). Smoothing is in DAYS by construction — there is no intraday smoothing constant here, because there is no intraday output to smooth.
paramNotes.zClampSigmas: Robust-z clamp (shared convention with composite.readiness_score) so one extreme daily value moves the trend to the edge of the scale and no further.
paramNotes.bandNeutralHalfWidth: Half-width, in points either side of the neutral 50, of the band that reads as 'about your usual'. Coarse on purpose: the honest output of this engine is a direction, not a decimal.
paramNotes.moderateConfidenceCap: Hard ceiling on DerivedValue.confidence for a moderate-density trend. A daily trend built from sparse daytime sampling is a low-confidence reading by construction, and the cap is what makes that structural rather than a matter of copy.
paramNotes.denseConfidenceCap: The ceiling that would apply to vendor-dense data. Published now so the shape is fixed; unreachable in Phase 3 in practice.

algorithms.summaryEn: Epley estimated one-repetition maximum: weight * (1 + reps/30), computed per exercise from logged sets.

paramNotes.epleyDivisor: The published Epley constant. Stable, not provisional in itself — the entry is provisional because the reps cutoff and the choice of Epley over Brzycki are not yet settled.
paramNotes.maxRepsForEstimate: Above this rep count the estimate stops being meaningful, so no e1RM is emitted rather than one that overstates.

algorithms.summaryEn: Brzycki estimated one-repetition maximum: weight * 36 / (37 - reps), computed per exercise from logged sets. A second published formula alongside workout.strength.e1rm's Epley curve (EPIC-42/28) — shown side by side rather than one replacing the other, since the two diverge meaningfully at higher rep counts and neither is universally more accurate. Shares workout.strength.e1rm's producesMetricIds on purpose: the registry metric is method-agnostic (an estimated one-rep max), and algorithmId/algorithmVersion on the stored row is what says which formula produced it, the same way composite.readiness_score's 1.0.0/2.0.0 both produce readiness.score.

paramNotes.brzyckiConstant: The published Brzycki numerator constant. Stable, not provisional in itself.
paramNotes.brzyckiRepsCeiling: The formula's own singularity: at reps=37 the denominator hits zero, and beyond it the estimate goes negative. Never evaluated at or beyond this reps count, regardless of maxRepsForEstimate.
paramNotes.maxRepsForEstimate: Above this rep count Brzycki's estimate is widely considered to drift further than Epley's, so no estimate is emitted rather than one that overstates. Deliberately lower than workout.strength.e1rm's cap (12) for exactly that reason.

algorithms.summaryEn: Volume load: the sum of weight * reps across a session's working sets.

paramNotes.includeWarmupSets: 0 = exclude, 1 = include. Boolean-as-double because AlgorithmVersion.params is numeric-only on both platforms; do not widen the type for one flag.

algorithms.summaryEn: Flags a logged set that beats the previous best weight for that exercise, within the same rep-range bucket.

paramNotes.minImprovementFraction: PROVISIONAL. A floating-point tie must not fire a PR celebration every session.
paramNotes.lookbackDays: A stored record older than this no longer gates a new one, so a long-inactive PR does not stand forever as an unbeatable ceiling.
paramNotes._scope: As shipped (0.1.0), the comparison is weight-only within a (movement, rep-range) bucket — see docs/algorithms/strength.md. Detecting a PR by reps-at-a-given-weight, or by estimated 1RM (which would make workout.strength.e1rm a real input rather than an independent, separately-computed value), is a documented future extension, not yet built. inputMetricIds is empty rather than naming workout.strength.e1rm because nothing here reads an e1RM DerivedValue today.

algorithms.summaryEn: Sums the hydration ledger for a local day and expresses it against the user's own goal. The goal is user-set, not computed for them.

paramNotes.defaultGoalLitres: PROVISIONAL and a STARTING POINT ONLY, never presented as a medical recommendation. The user's own goal, once set, always wins.
paramNotes.goalPctCapPercent: Display clamp so an unusually heavy day does not render an alarming percentage.

algorithms.summaryEn: Descriptive-only arithmetic over period start and end dates the user recorded. Emits no prediction of any kind.

paramNotes.minCyclesForLengthEstimate: Two recorded starts are the minimum that can define one interval. Below this, no cycle.length is emitted.
paramNotes.maxPlausibleCycleDays: Intervals longer than this are treated as a gap in logging rather than one very long cycle, so a missed month does not distort the history.
paramNotes.scopeBoundary: There is deliberately NO fertile-window, ovulation, or next-period prediction entry in this file. Those are gated behind plan decisions A17/A18 and a retained clinical advisor (A25). Adding a predictive algorithm id here would be the whole gate failing quietly — it must arrive as its own reviewed entry, not as a params tweak to this one.

algorithms.summaryEn: Behaviour-vs-score association (EPIC-29). For one logged behaviour and one daily score, splits the days the user actually journaled into a behaviour-present arm and a behaviour-absent arm, then compares the NEXT DAY's score distribution between the two. Effect size is Cliff's delta and the interval is a percentile bootstrap — NON-PARAMETRIC throughout, because score distributions are skewed and n is small, so a t-test would be assuming a shape the data does not have. Below the minimum-n gates nothing is emitted at all (suppressed, with the shortfall reported); above them an interval spanning zero is reported honestly as 'no clear association' rather than withheld. Findings are association only; this algorithm makes no causal claim and no surface built on it may.

paramNotes.producesMetricIdsNote: The one id here is the NAMESPACE row registry.json defines (journal.correlation). Concrete finding ids extend it as journal.correlation.<behaviorId>.<scoreId> — one per behaviour x score pair the user has actually logged enough of. They are deliberately not enumerated in either contract: the set is a product of behaviors.json and the scored ids above, so enumerating it would create ~90 catalogue rows that carry no data and rot the moment a behaviour is added. The namespace row is what fixes the family's unit, sensitivity and bilingual identity; sensitiveClass=sensitivePlus on it is what marks every finding beneath it as lifestyle-revealing (I7).
paramNotes.lookbackDays: Trailing local days of journal history the engine analyses. Long enough that a fortnightly behaviour can clear the gates, short enough that a finding describes the person's current life rather than last year's.
paramNotes.minObservedDays: MANDATORY GATE, plan §11 EPIC-29. Minimum OBSERVED days (both arms combined, each paired with a next-day score) before any comparison is made. An observed day is one the user journaled at all — a day with no journal activity is not evidence the behaviour was absent, and counting it as absence would be inventing data. Below this the finding is SUPPRESSED, not shown with a caveat.
paramNotes.minDaysPerArm: MANDATORY GATE. Minimum days in EACH arm (with / without). A 20-day sample that is 19 with and 1 without describes nothing, and an effect size computed over it would look identical on screen to one computed over a balanced sample.
paramNotes.bootstrapIterations: Resamples drawn for the percentile confidence interval. 2000 is the published count; the interval's endpoints are reported to two decimals, and 2000 resamples put the Monte-Carlo noise on a percentile well below that resolution.
paramNotes.bootstrapSeed: FIXED, published seed for the deterministic splitmix64 generator both platforms implement. A bootstrap is random by nature, so an unseeded one would give a slightly different interval on every recompute and a different interval on each platform — a finding that changes when you reopen the app is not a finding. The value itself is arbitrary (the epic number); what is load-bearing is that it never changes.
paramNotes.ciLowerPercentile: Lower percentile of the resampled Cliff's-delta distribution. With ciUpperPercentile this is a 95% percentile-method interval. The exact index rule is published in docs/algorithms/correlations.md and is part of the cross-platform contract, not an implementation detail.
paramNotes.ciUpperPercentile: Upper percentile. An interval that straddles zero is the 'no clear association' outcome, which is reported, never hidden.
paramNotes.negligibleDeltaThreshold: |delta| below this reads as a negligible effect. Romano et al. (2006) thresholds for Cliff's delta, used ONLY to pick the strength word in copy and never to gate whether a finding is shown — the interval decides that.
paramNotes.smallDeltaThreshold: |delta| below this reads as a small effect.
paramNotes.mediumDeltaThreshold: |delta| below this reads as a medium effect; at or above it, large.
paramNotes.confidenceFullNDays: Paired-day count at which the sample-size half of the confidence factor saturates. Confidence is sampleFactor x precisionFactor (see the doc); it is NOT a p-value and is never rendered as one.
paramNotes.contextCeilingNote: The confidence ceiling applied when the window overlaps a declared ContextStatus is NOT duplicated here. It lives once, in ContextAnnotator.activeContextConfidenceCeiling, alongside the caveat sentences it belongs with — two copies of one number is exactly the drift this contract exists to prevent (same rule stress.day_trend follows for madToSigma).
paramNotes.noParametricConstants: There is deliberately no alpha, no critical value, no assumed-sigma and no normality constant in this block. If one ever appears here, the method changed from the published non-parametric one and needs a semver bump and a doc rewrite, not a params tweak.
